title: iOS 1.0 — The iPhone & iPad app launches
iOS 1.1 — Cross-section layers, alternates and timing scenarios
body:
- New cross-section & map layers — GRAMET/Windy/ForeFlight presets, DWD & Met Office synoptic front charts, current-conditions overlay.
- tabbed briefing (Advisory/Discussion/Cross-Section/Map), cross-section color themes, offline packs, cache-first cold start
- Weather alternates — regulatory alternate-requirement assessment (FAA + EASA) with weather-based airport suggestions.
- Timing Scenarios — scan adjacent days to find a better-weather departure window.
- Options to improve — actionable advisory mitigations (altitude levers, VFR corridors) that never change the grade.
- Sun & night awareness — sunrise/sunset markers, into-the-sun sectors, night shading.
- Convective insight — model-vs-diagnostic cross-check and VFR-avoidability character.

title: iOS 1.2 — Briefing notifications, Siri and seamless updates
body:
- Briefing update notifications — Opt in to be notified when a flight's briefing changes, with per-flight control (Default / Always / Mute) and an account setting for how often.
- Siri, Shortcuts & Spotlight — Open a flight's briefing by voice or from search.
- Seamless forecast updates — The flight list and any open briefing quietly sync to the latest forecast on open, on pull-to-refresh, and when you return to the app — with a live "Updating…" indicator.
- Smoother flight creation — Routes typed with airway/SID/Field-15 syntax are interpreted before saving, future flights beyond the forecast horizon open cleanly, and accidental double-submits are prevented.
- Clearer weather display — Wind directions and headings are zero-padded to three digits, plus cloud-layer fixes for more accurate cross-sections.

title: iOS 1.3 — Flight sharing, the European forecast map and debriefs
body:
- Share a flight: send any flight to another pilot with a link. They can subscribe and follow your briefing read-only.
- European forecast map: a new pan-European overview map with tap-to-open airport cards, plus an airport forecast overlay right on the briefing route map.
- Rate your briefings: thumbs up / thumbs down feedback on the weather digest, and a new post-flight debrief to tell us how the forecast held up.
- Smarter timing: flights now show how much timing flexibility the latest forecast data gives you, and the flight list refreshes automatically when you return to it.
- Clearer advisories: advisories now explain why a region fired, not just how severe it is. Convective grading is sharper, and missing data is flagged distinctly instead of appearing green.
- iPad polish: native tab bar and smoother scrolling on iPad.

title: iOS 1.4 — Route SIGMETs, observations and approach feasibility
body:
- Route SIGMETs — area hazards along your route now show in the briefing, with tappable detail
- Current Observations — a table of METARs from the nearest airports, capped to the 10 closest on iPhone
- New approach-feasibility advisory — flags when the published approach isn't aligned with the runway the wind favours, and you can now declare your own unpublished cloud-break procedures
- Sharper thunderstorm detection in Europe (ICON-D2 explicit convection) and high-resolution HRRR forecasts on US routes
- Flight list — swipe to delete, a red dot marks briefings you haven't opened, plus sharing polish
- iPad — the forecast map now has a sidebar toggle so it can't strand you
- Cross-section legend redesigned for colour-blind readability; cleaner icing advisories and airport card layout
